# Preserved RTL word-order failure

`rtl-word-order.pdf` is a generated, one-page experimental semantic PDF retained
as negative reader evidence. It contains 64 copies of `سلام` separated by ASCII
spaces (319 Unicode scalars), shaped at 24 pt with Noto Sans Arabic, ligatures
enabled, automatic direction, and zero page rotation.

It was generated by the native `shaped-text-probe --semantic-long` experiment
with exact Type3 definition reuse, before the RTL boundary refusal was added.
The current semantic serializer deliberately refuses this input. The PDF's
visible vectors and unused embedded font preserve that original experiment;
this fixture is not a supported semantic document or production UI fixture.

PDFium's first logical `س` receives the leftmost word's x=73.992004 pt box even
though the first native source occurrence belongs at x=3290.012 pt. Identical
repeated words conceal that reversed word order in copied Unicode. The complete
four-rotation negative report is
[`semantic-long-rtl-words-negative.json`](../../../../docs/semantic-long-rtl-words-negative.json).

Run the isolated separator experiment from the repository root:

```powershell
python -B scripts/probe-semantic-rtl-separators.py
```

The probe defaults to this checked-in fixture, changes only the ToUnicode space
mapping in new copies under ignored artifacts, and records the source and
PDFium DLL SHA256 values. It does not modify this PDF or reshape substituted
text. The measured results are summarized in
[`semantic-rtl-separator-probe.json`](../../../../docs/semantic-rtl-separator-probe.json).

The embedded original font is the unmodified sibling
[`NotoSansArabic-Regular.ttf`](../NotoSansArabic-Regular.ttf), copyright
2015–2021 Google LLC, distributed under the
[`SIL Open Font License 1.1`](../LICENSE_NOTO.txt).
The existing [font provenance](../provenance.json) records its upstream pinned
source and version. This directory's [provenance.json](provenance.json) records
the PDF, font, and reader hashes and generation parameters. Only this one
negative PDF is retained; other generated evidence remains under artifacts.
